description: Standalone golden for calc_heat_axisym.py (Cubit-free, uniform-q).  Locks the 2D-axisymmetric thermal solver and its 2*pi*r surface integral INDEPENDENTLY of the EM chain.  test_heat_chain_golden.py's axisym leg exercises the cross-mesh spatial projection, but it SKIPS when the coil STEP sample (ih_peec_bem_coarse_coil.step) is absent -- so the axisym solver had no CI-runnable golden until this one.
cross_check: q_surf_int_W == q_uniform_Wm2 * surface_area_m2 (analytic: uniform flux over the 2*pi*r-weighted lateral surface).  Locks the axisym surface integral to <1e-6 relative.
notes: Cubit-free: --q-uniform short-circuits the cross-mesh projection so no EM reference run / coil STEP is needed; runs in CI on an 81-element / 361-DOF Q2 mesh.
Complements test_heat_chain_golden.py, whose axisym leg covers the cross-mesh spatial projection but skips without ih_peec_bem_coarse_coil.step.
surface_area 0.0039270 m2 = 2*pi*R*H lateral area of the R=0.025 H=0.025 cylinder; q_surf_int = 1e4 * that = 39.27 W.

The committed default-order regression explicitly passes --fes-order 2: 361 temperature DOFs on the 9x9 Q2 quad grid, while the serialized mesh geometry remains order 1 and is not re-curved after load.
Solve is a direct sparsecholesky on a fixed committed mesh, so values are reproducible to ~machine precision; the 1e-3 K / 0.5% bands absorb cross-platform float noise.
